summary: All four attestations are already represented; no added example or new sense is justified.
The translator and translated content may be expressed, omitted or relativised. Source language is m-Kurdish; target is l-Syriac. In the Infinitiv, dani encodes the content genitively.
11/307 has an Infectum translation verb followed by an Infectum-wa telling verb; preserve their morphological distinction despite the German past rendering.
The source entry files mtarǧamle/mtarǧəm under I. Preserve that label, including the inherited warning about the Syriac etymology; the present evidence does not resolve borrowing history.
Preserve inherited stem I for the m-prefixed quadriliteral and the etymological warning; do not silently relabel it Q or II.

New Infectum-wa mtarǧamnowo and Preterit-wa mtarǧamwole separate subject indexing and -wo placement. gədmtarǧamle is conjectural Infectum in 1184, not an assertion that either named author actually translated a Syriac Quran.
In 2933 recipient -le/-li precedes content -yo; both tokens remain separately decided but only one quotation is added.
In 3621–3622 and 415, -i- plus l-agent marks translated content. The English have translated at 415 does not make the Turoyo Detransitive.
Unnumbered inherited examples all serve the sole active sense 1 (Preterit 1, Infectum 2, Infinitiv 1). Additions fill the first two cells to five, counting the paired 2933 quotation once.
The inherited head questions the Syriac etymology. These four translation contexts cannot determine its historical source; retain the question for comparative research.
Check the missing target after lu and the unfinished u in Jan 1.10/371; the new Infectum-wa witness retains the source omissions.
Does lu Ǧan həwile mtarǧəme at Jan 3.2/33 mean that Jan translated the documents or had them translated? No causative meaning is asserted.
Confirm feminine mtarǧəmo with kṯawto at 2.23/4031 and the status of unmarked mtarǧəm at 4.I/446 as Detransitive Preterit versus a result predicate.
Confirm the active Preterit analysis of Mtarǧəmili at 4.I/415 by comparison with 2.17/3622; no Detransitive example is selected from it.
Should lexical result noun tərǧomo at 2.17/3657 be kept outside the syntactic Infinitiv box? The inherited process nominal turǧomo is unchanged.
Check printed u qara at 3.14/132 against qarar; preserve its source spelling rather than supply the final consonant.
Source languages include Turkish and French, targets Turkish and Syriac; the m-source/l-target frame retains sense 1. Swedish is a book’s prior language in 446, not an overt m-source argument.
